response.prompt: Rate the Annotation Quality based on each of the following categories.
questionOptions: Is the annotation targeting the right visual element and correctly placed?
Is the annotation clearly visible without overlap or blurriness?
Is the annotation relevant and accurate for the annotation task?
Is the original chart preserved while adding these annotations?
Are the annotations stylistically consistent with the original chart design?

parameters.taskPrompt: Add visual annotations to highlight three significant waves: (1) Add a vertical shaded grey region at the left side of the chart with label 'Jan. 2021 peak' at the top marking the initial peak period, (2) Add a vertical shaded grey region in the middle-right area with label 'Delta wave' at the top marking the Delta variant surge around August-October 2021, and (3) Add a vertical shaded grey region at the far right with label 'Omicron wave' at the top marking the Omicron surge in late 2021 to early 2022. The labels should be positioned above the chart area. Return the annotated image.

Add visual annotations to highlight two significant events: (1) Add a vertical dashed line at October 2018 with a text callout above showing 'Oct. 2, 2018' as the header and 'Journalist Jamal Khashoggi is killed in Saudi Consulate in Istanbul' as the description, and (2) Add a vertical dashed line at October 2021 with a text callout above showing 'Oct. 7, 2021' as the header and 'U.N. Human Rights Council ends war crimes probe in Yemen' as the description. The text callouts should be positioned above the chart data area with the date in bold. Return the annotated image.

Add the following annotations: (1) Add a label '20th century average' with a bracket or line pointing to the zero baseline (horizontal axis), (2) Add 'Warmer' label with an upward arrow indicator near the top-left of the y-axis, (3) Add 'Cooler' label with a downward arrow indicator near the bottom-left of the y-axis. Return the annotated image.

Add the following annotations: (1) Add a vertical dashed line at February 24, 2022 with a label 'Feb. 24' and annotation 'Russia invades Ukraine' pointing to the date when the invasion occurred (the flow was still high at this point), (2) Add a shaded region with label 'Maintenance shutdowns' around July-August 2022 highlighting the period when gas flow dropped significantly and had multiple shutdowns. Return the annotated image.

Add the following annotations: (1) Add a vertical reference line at approximately 1996 with the label 'OxyContin painkiller introduced', (2) Add a numbered callout '1. Deaths of despair were declining until the opioid epidemic hit' with an arrow pointing to the early 1980s dip in the All line, (3) Add a numbered callout '2. The downward trend ended earlier among middle-aged whites' with an arrow pointing to the mid-1990s where the Whites line starts rising, (4) Add a dashed line labeled 'Pre-1990s trend' extending from the 1979 starting point of the All line forward to show what the trajectory would have been without the opioid crisis. Return the annotated image.

Identify the category with the highest value (B = 55) and add an arrow pointing to it with a text annotation marking it as the maximum. Also draw a reference line at the average value across all three categories.

Identify the category with the highest value (D = 91) and the most negative value (C = -33). Add arrows pointing to each and add text annotations labeling them as 'Maximum' and 'Minimum' respectively.

Add a downward-sloping trend arrow from the upper-left to lower-right and label it 'Negative correlation: more HP = less MPG'. Also label the most fuel-efficient outlier near 46 MPG with an arrow and text 'Most efficient: ~46 MPG'.

Annotate the chart by: (1) Adding a text label at x=3 (where the line breaks) stating 'Missing value at x=3', (2) Adding a text label at x=5 stating 'Missing value at x=5', and (3) Adding a reference line or arrow connecting the two valid points on either side of each gap to indicate the expected interpolation path if data were available.

Add an arrow pointing to the B-predicted-as-C cell (count=6) with a text label 'Main error: 6 B→C misclassifications'. Add a text annotation near class A's row noting 'Class A: perfect classification (13/13)'. Add a reference line or enclosure highlighting the off-diagonal cells to emphasize the error pattern.
Annotate these two points with arrows and labels showing the dominant series and its percentage share.
Add text labels near the axes where each category strongly outperforms the other, noting the advantage.
